# konnect_event_gateway_cluster_policy_request_rule_validator (Resource)

EventGatewayClusterPolicyRequestRuleValidator Resource

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "konnect_event_gateway_cluster_policy_request_rule_validator" "my_eventgatewayclusterpolicyrequestrulevalidator" {
  condition = "context.auth.principal.name == \"this-user\""
  config = {
    requests = [
      {
        consumer_group_heartbeat = {
          rules = [
            {
              action      = "passthrough"
              description = "...my_description..."
              rule        = "context.group.id.startsWith('team-a.')"
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  }
  description = ""
  enabled     = true
  gateway_id  = "9524ec7d-36d9-465d-a8c5-83a3c9390458"
  labels = {
    key = "value"
  }
  name               = "...my_name..."
  virtual_cluster_id = "14fdb46c-b44c-45b7-974e-c5643ecb64db"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `config` (Attributes) The configuration of the request rule validator policy. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config))
- `gateway_id` (String) The UUID of your Gateway.
- `virtual_cluster_id` (String) The ID of the Virtual Cluster.

### Optional

- `condition` (String) A string containing the boolean expression that determines whether the policy is applied. Default: ""
- `description` (String) A human-readable description of the policy. Default: ""
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the policy is enabled. Default: true
- `labels` (Map of String) Labels store metadata of an entity that can be used for filtering an entity list or for searching across entity types. 

Keys must be of length 1-63 characters, and cannot start with "kong", "konnect", "mesh", "kic", or "_".
- `name` (String) A unique user-defined name of the policy.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) An ISO-8601 timestamp representation of entity creation date.
- `id` (String) The unique identifier of the policy.
- `parent_policy_id` (String) The unique identifier of the parent policy, if any.
- `updated_at` (String) An ISO-8601 timestamp representation of entity update date.

<a id="nestedatt--config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config`

Required:

- `requests` (Attributes List) The rules to apply, grouped by Kafka request type. A request type can occur more than
once in this list. Every entry for the type applies, in list order.
Requests of a type that is not in this list are not validated.
A maximum of 100 entries are allowed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--requests))

<a id="nestedatt--config--requests"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config.requests`

Optional:

- `alter_client_quotas` (Attributes) The rules to apply to Kafka `AlterClientQuotas` requests. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--requests--alter_client_quotas))
- `alter_configs` (Attributes) The rules to apply to Kafka `AlterConfigs` requests. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--requests--alter_configs))
- `alter_user_scram_credentials` (Attributes) The rules to apply to Kafka `AlterUserScramCredentials` requests. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--requests--alter_user_scram_credentials))
- `consumer_group_heartbeat` (Attributes) The rules to apply to Kafka `ConsumerGroupHeartbeat` requests. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--requests--consumer_group_heartbeat))
- `create_partitions` (Attributes) The rules to apply to Kafka `CreatePartitions` requests. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--requests--create_partitions))
- `create_topics` (Attributes) The rules to apply to Kafka `CreateTopics` requests.

When at least one `create_topics` rule is configured, Event Gateway turns auto topic
creation off on `Metadata` requests, because clients could use it to bypass the rules. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--requests--create_topics))
- `fetch` (Attributes) The rules to apply to Kafka `Fetch` requests. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--requests--fetch))
- `incremental_alter_configs` (Attributes) The rules to apply to Kafka `IncrementalAlterConfigs` requests. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--requests--incremental_alter_configs))
- `join_group` (Attributes) The rules to apply to Kafka `JoinGroup` requests. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--requests--join_group))
- `offset_commit` (Attributes) The rules to apply to Kafka `OffsetCommit` requests. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--requests--offset_commit))
- `offset_fetch` (Attributes) The rules to apply to Kafka `OffsetFetch` requests. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--requests--offset_fetch))
- `produce` (Attributes) The rules to apply to Kafka `Produce` requests. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--requests--produce))
- `txn_offset_commit` (Attributes) The rules to apply to Kafka `TxnOffsetCommit` requests. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--requests--txn_offset_commit))

<a id="nestedatt--config--requests--alter_client_quotas"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config.requests.alter_client_quotas`

Required:

- `rules` (Attributes List) Every rule in this list is evaluated independently against each quota operation in the request.
A rule that evaluates to `false` runs its action.
A maximum of 10 rules are allowed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--requests--alter_client_quotas--rules))

<a id="nestedatt--config--requests--alter_client_quotas--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config.requests.alter_client_quotas.rules`

Required:

- `action` (String) What to do when a rule evaluates to `false`.

`reject` fails the request with the `POLICY_VIOLATION` error code.
`passthrough` lets the request continue, but logs the violation in the same way as `reject`.
possible known values include one of ["reject", "passthrough"]
- `description` (String) An explanation of the rule. Event Gateway writes this text to the logs when the request
violates the rule, because the rule expression alone does not show the intent.
- `rule` (String) A boolean expression that describes the valid state of the request.
The action runs when the expression evaluates to `false`.
An expression that cannot be evaluated, for example because a value has an unexpected
format, also counts as `false`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = konnect_event_gateway_cluster_policy_request_rule_validator.my_konnect_event_gateway_cluster_policy_request_rule_validator
  id = jsonencode({
    gateway_id         = "9524ec7d-36d9-465d-a8c5-83a3c9390458"
    id                 = "9524ec7d-36d9-465d-a8c5-83a3c9390458"
    virtual_cluster_id = "..."
  })
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import konnect_event_gateway_cluster_policy_request_rule_validator.my_konnect_event_gateway_cluster_policy_request_rule_validator '{"gateway_id": "9524ec7d-36d9-465d-a8c5-83a3c9390458", "id": "9524ec7d-36d9-465d-a8c5-83a3c9390458", "virtual_cluster_id": "..."}'
```
